title: Unraveling the Mechanism of Phase Segregation Phenomena in IGZO Compounds via Precession Electron Diffraction and In-Situ TEM
content: In-Ga-Zn-O (IGZO) compounds are semiconducting oxides with huge potential in applications as channels in Thin Film Transistors (TFTs), enabling 3-dimensional integration of memory devices [1]. In IGZO TFTs the crystallographic configuration of the IGZO film is crucial in determining the overall device characteristics. For example, amorphous IGZO TFTs have relatively high electron mobility, similar to the polycrystalline IGZO phase, but suffer from low stability. In the stable crystallographic phase, IGZO exists in two polytypes having spaces group R3̅m (160) and P63/mmc (194). Beside this, there are many other possible crystallographic phases, which can be induced in IGZO tailoring the deposition conditions in combination with thermal treatments. Recently, we have demonstrated the formation of a spinel IGZO phase, which can be produced exploiting a spinel Ga-Zn-O (GZO) thin film as a seed layer prior to the deposition of the IGZO [2]. It has been shown that spinel IGZO is less prone to O-vacancies formation, a factor which determines the free electron density and thus the overall stability of IGZO-based devices.
